# Next-day consumption: French household (UCI, Sceaux) (Phase 4A)

*Generated by `python -m solvia.pipeline --steps model_consumption_france`. Validation split only; the test split is untouched until Phase 5.*

Training rows 709, validation rows 352. Target: kWh on the next day. 25 features (all from the past or the calendar).

## Selected: `ridge`

Validation MAE **4.566 kWh/day** (RMSE 5.769, R² 0.555, MAPE 18.4 % on days ≥ 1 kWh), **5.4 % lower MAE than the best baseline** (`baseline_mean_7d`).

## All baselines and models (validation)

| model | kind | mae | rmse | r2 | nmae | mape_pct | skill_vs_best_baseline_pct |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| ridge | model | 4.566 | 5.769 | 0.555 | 0.175 | 18.4 | +5.4 % |
| random_forest | model | 4.592 | 5.780 | 0.553 | 0.176 | 19.5 | +4.8 % |
| baseline_mean_7d | baseline | 4.825 | 6.398 | 0.452 | 0.185 | 19.7 | +0.0 % |
| hist_gradient_boosting | model | 5.158 | 6.533 | 0.429 | 0.198 | 21.8 | -6.9 % |
| baseline_last_week | baseline | 5.825 | 7.659 | 0.215 | 0.224 | 24.5 | -20.7 % |
| baseline_yesterday | baseline | 6.316 | 8.062 | 0.130 | 0.242 | 24.5 | -30.9 % |

`mae`, `rmse` in kWh/day; `nmae` = MAE / mean actual; skill = MAE reduction vs the best baseline.

## Prediction interval (10th–90th percentile)

Quantile HistGradientBoosting (`hist_gradient_boosting` settings): 54.8% of validation days fall inside the interval (target 80 %), mean width 9.02 kWh.

**Conformal adjustment** (computed on validation): each end is moved out by +2.68 kWh, giving 80.7% coverage on validation (80 % by construction, so not evidence) and a mean width of 14.38 kWh. The honest check is the test coverage in Phase 5.

## Experiment: target-day weather as a stand-in for a forecast (labelled)

Adding `t2m_target_day`, `hdd_target_day` changes validation MAE from 4.566 to 4.592 kWh/day. EXPERIMENT ONLY: uses the observed weather of the target day as a stand-in for a weather forecast; a real forecast is less accurate, so this is an upper bound on what forecasts could add.

## Tuning (expanding-window CV over whole training days)

| model | best parameters | CV MAE (kWh) | MAE per fold, earliest first |
|---|---|---|---|
| ridge | {'model__alpha': 100.0} | 5.098 | [4.778, 5.557, 5.425, 4.249, 5.482] |
| random_forest | {'model__max_features': 0.33, 'model__min_samples_leaf': 5} | 5.256 | [4.645, 5.664, 5.232, 5.178, 5.558] |
| hist_gradient_boosting | {'model__learning_rate': 0.05, 'model__max_leaf_nodes': 31, 'model__min_samples_leaf': 20} | 6.131 | [5.753, 6.822, 6.68, 5.352, 6.047] |

The first fold trains on the shortest history; a model that is much worse there than on later folds is sensitive to how much history it has seen (linear models extrapolate when the season changes).

Files: `reports/metrics/consumption_france_*.{csv,json}`, `models/consumption_france.joblib` + `.json`.
